terms.comment: Ancient diplōma is an official travel document, commeātus leave to come and go.

phrases.latin: Hoc est commeātūs diplōma, in quō nōmen meum est et imāgō.
phrases.english: This is a passport, with my name and my picture in it.

phrases.latin: Sine diplōmate nēmō in āëroplanum admittitur.
phrases.english: Nobody is let onto a plane without a passport.

sources: Lewis & Short: diploma · Lewis & Short: commeatus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 217.

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
